analysis.investment_thesis: Identixweb is a tiny ₹9 Cr revenue Shopify app developer — outside my circle of competence in consumer retail/FMCG, and too small and unproven to be a steady compounder. Despite debt-free balance sheet and strong ROCE of 34.3%, the business lacks scale, moat, and the predictable demand profile I require.
key_strengths: Zero borrowings across all 3 years and equity jumped to ₹31 Cr — fortress balance sheet
Promoter holding healthy at 62.99%, above my 55% threshold
key_risks: Revenue only ₹9 Cr — microcap with no proven track record through a downturn
IT services/Shopify apps — platform-dependent, no consumer moat, outside my domain
FCF negative in 2024 (-₹4 Cr) and 2025 (-₹2 Cr) despite tiny scale
red_flags: Reserves swung from ₹5 Cr → ₹3 Cr → ₹21 Cr — suggests recent equity raise diluting the story
Investing CF persistently negative (-₹3, -₹5, -₹5 Cr) with unclear returns
Net profit flat at ₹3 Cr in 2024 and 2025 despite revenue growth — margin sustainability unclear
analysis.detailed_analysis:
I built DMart by sticking to businesses I understand deeply — retail shelves, inventory turns, footfalls. A Shopify app developer with ₹9 Cr revenue and a ₹90 Cr market cap is the opposite of what I buy. It's a platform-dependent IT shop where one policy change by Shopify could wipe out the business model, and there is no evidence of a durable franchise. The headline ROE of 24.8% looks attractive but is on a tiny base; post the recent equity raise (reserves ballooning to ₹21 Cr), return ratios will compress meaningfully.

Balance sheet discipline is genuinely good — zero debt, promoter at 63% — but that alone does not make a compounder. P/E of 18.6x on ₹3 Cr PAT with negative free cash flow, no dividend history, and unproven earnings durability is not a reasonable price for quality in my book. I'd rather pay up for a proven consumer franchise than buy a cheap-looking SME IT microcap. Pass.
